    networks: [web]

  recs:
    build:
      context: ./services/recs
    image: acme/recs:dev
    command: >
      uvicorn recs.api:app
      --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8081
      --reload --reload-dir /code/recs
    environment:
      MODEL_URI: s3://acme-ml-models/recs/two-tower/2026-11-01/
      FEATURE_STORE_URL: redis://redis:6379/2
      EMBEDDING_DIM: 128
      AB_TEST_BUCKETS: '{"control": 50, "two_tower_v3": 50}'
      FALLBACK_STRATEGY: bestsellers
      LOG_LEVEL: debug
    ports: [ "8081:8081" ]
    volumes:
      - ./services/recs:/code
    depends_on:
      - redis
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {cpus: '2.0', memory: 3g}
        reservations:
          memory: 1g
    networks: [web]

  marketing:
    <<: *node-defaults
    build: ./apps/marketing
    ports:
      - target: 4321
        published: "4321"
        protocol: tcp
    environment:
      PUBLIC_SITE_URL: http://localhost:4321
      PUBLIC_GA_ID: G-XXXXXXXXXX
      PUBLIC_BANNER_TEXT: "🎄 Holiday Sale: up to 40% off — ends Dec 26!"
      PUBLIC_CMS_URL: http://localhost:1337
    labels:
      com.acme.team: "marketing-web"
      com.acme.owner: '@acme/growth-eng'

  search:
    image: getmeili/meilisearch:v1.11
    environment:
      - MEILI_MASTER_KEY=${MEILI_MASTER_KEY:-dev-only-master-key-change-me}
      - MEILI_ENV=development
      - MEILI_NO_ANALYTICS=true
    ports: ['7700:7700']
    volumes: [ "meili:/meili_data" ]
    networks:
      web:
        aliases: [ search.local ]

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:latest
    profiles: ["debug"]
    ports:
      - "8025:8025"
      - "1025:1025"
    environment:
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ACCEPT_ANY: 1
      MP_SMTP_AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE: 1
    networks: [web]


volumes:
  pgdata: {}
  cms-uploads:
  storefront-next:
  meili:
    driver: local

networks:
  web:
    name: acme-web
    driver: bridge

name: Storefront CI

# Lint/test on every PR that touches the storefront or the shared packages.
# Lighthouse + Chromatic on PRs only, Vercel preview per PR, prod deploy on `storefront@x.y.z` tags.
# Owner: @acme/web-platform   (ping #web-ci if main is red for > 1h)

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, 'release/**' ]
    tags: [ "storefront@*" ]
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'apps/storefront/**'
      - "packages/ui/**"
      - packages/pricing/**
      - '!**/*.md'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_lighthouse:
        description: 'Run Lighthouse against the preview URL?'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      locale:
        description: Locale to audit
        type: choice
        options: [en-NL, nl-NL, de-DE, 'fr-FR']
        default: en-NL

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  deployments: write

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  PNPM_VERSION: 9.12.1
  NODE_VERSION: "20"
  TURBO_TEAM: acme-web
  TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TURBO_TOKEN }}
  NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: 1
  FORCE_COLOR: "3"

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint & typecheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: ${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: ESLint
        run: pnpm turbo run lint --filter=@acme/storefront... --filter=@acme/ui
      - name: tsc
        run: pnpm turbo run typecheck --filter=...[origin/main]
      - name: Stylelint (CSS modules)
        run: pnpm stylelint "apps/storefront/**/*.module.css" --max-warnings=0

  test:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
        node: [ 18, 20, 22 ]
        shard: [1/3, 2/3, 3/3]
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            node: 20
            shard: 1/1
        exclude:
          - node: 18
            shard: 3/3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with: {version: "${{ env.PNPM_VERSION }}"}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: 'pnpm'
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Unit tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        run: pnpm --filter @acme/storefront test -- --shard=${{ matrix.shard }} --coverage
        env:
          TZ: Europe/Amsterdam   # price cut-off tests depend on CET midnight
          CI: true
      - name: Upload coverage
        if: matrix.node == 20 && matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          flags: storefront,shard-${{ strategy.job-index }}

  preview:
    needs: test
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: preview
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
    outputs:
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Deploy to Vercel (preview)
        id: deploy
        run: |
          npm i -g vercel@39
          url=$(vercel deploy --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} --scope acme-web --build-env NEXT_PUBLIC_CURRENCY=EUR)
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        env:
          VERCEL_ORG_ID: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          VERCEL_PROJECT_ID: prj_storefront_9f2a

  lighthouse:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || inputs.run_lighthouse
    needs: [preview]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Lighthouse CI
        id: lhci
        uses: treosh/lighthouse-ci-action@v12
        with:
          urls: |
            ${{ needs.preview.outputs.url }}/
            ${{ needs.preview.outputs.url }}/c/womens-sneakers
            ${{ needs.preview.outputs.url }}/p/aurora-runner-2?sku=AUR-2-BLK-42
          budgetPath: ./apps/storefront/lighthouse-budget.json
          uploadArtifacts: true
          temporaryPublicStorage: true
      - name: Comment scores on the PR
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          LH_MANIFEST: ${{ steps.lhci.outputs.manifest }}
        with:
          # fmt: js
          script: |
            const manifest = JSON.parse(process.env.LH_MANIFEST)
            const pct = (x) => Math.round(x*100)
            const rows = manifest.map(r => { const s=r.summary; return `| ${new URL(r.url).pathname} | ${pct(s.performance)} | ${pct(s.accessibility)} | ${pct(s.seo)} |` })
            const body = ['### 🔦 Lighthouse (mobile, ${{ inputs.locale || 'en-NL' }})', '', '| page | perf | a11y | seo |', '|---|--:|--:|--:|', ...rows].join('\n')
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({ ...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number, body })

  chromatic:
    needs: lint
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'skip-visual') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0     # chromatic needs full history for baselines
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - uses: chromaui/action@latest
        with:
          projectToken: ${{ secrets.CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
          workingDir: packages/ui
          onlyChanged: true
          exitZeroOnChanges: true
          autoAcceptChanges: "main"

  deploy-prod:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/storefront@')
    needs: [test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npx vercel@39 deploy --prod --token=${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
      - name: Draft GitHub release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          draft: true
          name: Storefront ${{ github.ref_name }}
          # fmt: markdown
          body: |
            ## 🛍️ Storefront ${{ github.ref_name }}
            Deployed to **production** by @${{ github.actor }}.
            * [Vercel deployment](https://vercel.com/acme-web/storefront)
            * [Lighthouse report](https://lighthouse.acme-shop.example/storefront/${{ github.sha }}) -- compare against the last tag before you celebrate

            > Remember to update the price feed in Merchant Center if SKUs or prices changed!
      - name: Notify #launches
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.27.0
        with:
          channel-id: C04ACMEWEB
          slack-message: "*Storefront ${{ github.ref_name }}* is live :tada: <https://www.acme-shop.example|acme-shop.example>"
        env:
          SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN }}

# shop-web: storefront + recs manifests (prod-eu-west)
# Originally generated by kompose, hand-maintained ever since. Sorry.
# Apply with:  kubectl apply -f kubernetes_multi_document.yaml --server-side
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shop-web
  labels:
    team: web-platform
    istio-injection: enabled
--- # ---------------- config ----------------
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: recs-config
  namespace: shop-web
data:
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
  RECS_MAX_ITEMS: "24"
  RECS_FALLBACK_STRATEGY: bestsellers
  ENABLE_PERSONALIZATION: "true"
  # fmt: json
  feature-flags.json: |
    {"pdp_carousel": {"enabled": true, "variant": "two_tower_v3", "rollout": 0.5},
     "cart_upsell": {"enabled": true,"max_items":4},
       "email_recs": {"enabled": false, "note": "waiting on the CRM consent flag"}}
  slots.yaml: |
    # rendered into the storefront at build time
    slots:
      - id: pdp-similar
        title: "You might also like"
        max: 12
      - id: cart-upsell
        title: Complete the look ✨
        max: 4
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: storefront-secrets
  namespace: shop-web
  annotations:
    # rotated by vault-agent, do NOT edit by hand
    vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: 'true'
type: Opaque
stringData:
  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: "sk_live_REPLACED_BY_VAULT"
  CMS_API_TOKEN: replaced-by-vault
  PREVIEW_SECRET: >-
    replaced-by-vault
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: storefront
  namespace: shop-web
  labels: &storefront-labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: storefront
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: acme-shop
    app.kubernetes.io/version: "4.12.0"
spec:
  replicas: 6
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate: {maxSurge: 25%, maxUnavailable: 0}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: storefront
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *storefront-labels
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
        prometheus.io/port: '9464'
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: storefront}
      containers:
      - name: storefront
        image: registry.acme.example/web/storefront:4.12.0@sha256:3f1c9a7e2b4d6f8091a2b3c4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7a8
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
          name: http
        - {containerPort: 9464, name: metrics}
        envFrom:
          - configMapRef: { name: storefront-config }
          - secretRef:
              name: storefront-secrets
        env:
          - name: NODE_ENV
            value: production
          - name: NEXT_PUBLIC_CURRENCY
            value: "EUR"
          - name: RECS_URL
            value: http://recs.shop-web.svc.cluster.local:8081/v1
          - name: POD_IP
            valueFrom:
              fieldRef:
                fieldPath: status.podIP
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 250m, memory: 512Mi}
          limits:
            memory: 1Gi
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /api/health, port: http}
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /api/health?deep=0
            port: http
          initialDelaySeconds: 20
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 10"]
--- # svc
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: storefront, namespace: shop-web}
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: storefront
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shop-web
  namespace: shop-web
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: 8m
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet: |
      more_set_headers "X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN";
      if ($request_uri ~* "^/(sale|black-friday)/?$") { return 301 /c/deals; }
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/server-snippet: "location = /robots.txt { add_header Content-Type text/plain; return 200 'User-agent: *\nDisallow: /checkout\nDisallow: /cart\nSitemap: https://www.acme-shop.example/sitemap.xml\n'; }"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [www.acme-shop.example, acme-shop.example]
      secretName: shop-web-tls
  rules:
    - host: www.acme-shop.example
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend: {service: {name: storefront, port: {name: http}}}
          - path: /api/recs
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: recs
                port:
                  number: 8081
---
# PodDisruptionBudget moved to the platform repo (PLAT-2231); keeping the empty doc so diffs line up
...
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: storefront
  namespace: shop-web
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: storefront}
  minReplicas: 6
  maxReplicas: 40   # BF/CM weekend: bump to 80 by hand!!
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target: {type: Utilization,
               averageUtilization: 65}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: recs-retrain
  namespace: shop-web
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 2-5 * * *"
  timeZone: Europe/Amsterdam
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 2
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 1
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          containers:
            - name: retrain
              image: registry.acme.example/ml/recs-trainer:2026.11.3
              command: ["python", "-m", "recs.train"]
              args:
              - --model=two_tower_v3
              - "--since=P14D"
              - '--min-interactions=5'
              env:
                - {name: MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, value: "http://mlflow.ml.svc:5000"}
                - name: TRAIN_SQL
                  value: |
                    SELECT user_id, sku, event_type, ts
                    FROM events.product_interactions
                    WHERE ts > now() - interval '14 days'
                      AND event_type IN ('view','add_to_cart','purchase')

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Acme Storefront API
  version: "2026-11-01"
  summary: Catalog, pricing, cart & recommendations for the Acme web storefront.
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    The **Storefront API** backs `www.acme-shop.example`, the marketing landing pages and the mobile web app. It is a BFF ("backend for frontend"): it stitches together the headless CMS, the pricing engine and the recommendation service so the browser only ever talks to one origin.

    ## Conventions
    * Prices are **integer minor units** (cents), always paired with an ISO-4217 `currency`.
    * SKUs look like `AUR-2-BLK-42` → *family*-*generation*-*colour*-*size*.
    + Timestamps are RFC 3339, UTC.

    ## Rate limits
    plan | req/min | burst
    ---|---:|---:
    anonymous | 120 | 40
    logged-in | 600 | 100
    partner | 3000 | 500

    Questions? Ping `#storefront-api` on Slack or open an issue 🙏
  contact:
    name: Web Platform team
    email: web-platform@acme-shop.example
    url: https://handbook.acme-shop.example/storefront/
  license: {name: Proprietary, identifier: LicenseRef-Acme}
servers:
  - url: https://api.acme-shop.example/storefront/v2
    description: Production
  - url: https://api.staging.acme-shop.example/storefront/v2
    description: staging (reset every night at 03:00 CET)
  - url: http://localhost:{port}/v2
    description: Local docker compose
    variables:
      port:
        default: "3001"
        enum: ['3001', "3002"]
tags:
  - name: Catalog
    description: Products, variants (SKUs) and categories. Copy & images come from the CMS.
  - name: Pricing
    description: >
      Price lookups, including
      member prices and
      active promotions.
  - name: Cart
  - name: Recommendations
    description: "Personalised product carousels, backed by the `recs` service (two-tower model)."
    x-displayName: Recs ✨

paths:
  /products/{slug}:
    get:
      tags: [Catalog]
      operationId: getProduct
      summary: Get a product by slug
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Locale'
        - name: slug
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: { type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$', example: aurora-runner-2 }
        - name: include
          in: query
          description: Comma separated list of extra blocks. `reviews` is slow (≈300 ms p95), avoid it on listing pages.
          style: form
          explode: false
          schema:
            type: array
            items: {type: string, enum: [variants, reviews, related, cms_blocks]}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          headers:
            Cache-Control:
              schema: {type: string}
              example: "public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=600"
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Product"
              examples:
                sneaker:
                  summary: Sneaker with 2 variants, one sold out
                  value:
                    slug: aurora-runner-2
                    name: Aurora Runner 2
                    badges: ["new", "eco"]
                    variants:
                      - {sku: AUR-2-BLK-42, color: black, size: "42", price: {amount: 11995, currency: EUR, was: 12995}, stock: 14}
                      - {sku: AUR-2-WHT-43, color: white, size: "43", price: {amount: 11995, currency: EUR}, stock: 0}
        404:
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
        default:
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Problem"

  /prices:
    get:
      tags:
      - Pricing
      operationId: listPrices
      summary: Bulk price lookup (max. 100 SKUs)
      # fmt: markdown
      description: |-
        Returns the **current** sell price for each SKU, applying (in this order):
        1. member price, if the shopper is logged in and `member=true`
        2. the best active promotion (see `GET /promotions`)
        3. psychological rounding -- prices end in `,95` (NL/DE) or `.99` (UK)

        Unknown SKUs are silently dropped; check `missing[]` in the response.
      parameters:
        - in: query
          name: sku
          required: true
          schema:
            type: array
            maxItems: 100
            items:
              type: string
              pattern: "^[A-Z]{3}-\\d+-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9A-Z]{1,3}$"
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Locale'
        - {name: member, in: query, schema: {type: boolean, default: false}}
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Prices keyed by SKU.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  prices:
                    type: object
                    additionalProperties: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
                  missing: {type: array, items: {type: string}}
              example:
                prices:
                  AUR-2-BLK-42: {amount: 11995, currency: EUR, was: 12995, promo: BF26-10}
                  TEE-1-WHT-M: { amount: 2295, currency: EUR }
                  "HOM-MUG-SET4": {amount: 2999, currency: EUR, promo: ~}
                missing: [GFT-0-XXX-0]

  /cart/{cartId}/items:
    parameters:
      - {name: cartId, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string, format: uuid}}
    post:
      tags: [Cart]
      operationId: addCartItem
      security:
        - {}
        - cookieAuth: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [sku, quantity]
              properties:
                sku: {type: string, examples: ["AUR-2-BLK-42"]}
                quantity: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 10, default: 1}
                gift_wrap: {type: boolean, description: "+€4.95, not available for gift cards"}
      responses:
        '201': {description: Created, content: {application/json: {schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Cart'}}}}
        '409':
          description: Out of stock -- the item was **not** added.
        '422':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Problem'

  /recommendations:
    get:
      tags: [Recommendations]
      operationId: getRecommendations
      summary: Personalised carousel
      # fmt: markdown
      description: >-
        Returns up to `limit` products for a carousel `slot`. When the shopper has no history we fall back to bestsellers in the same category (see `strategy` in the response). Results are cached per (slot, segment) for 5 minutes, **not** per user -- so never put user-specific copy in the CMS carousel title.
      parameters:
        - name: slot
          in: query
          required: true
          schema: {type: string, enum: [pdp-similar, cart-upsell, home-for-you, email-digest]}
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 48, default: 12}
        - name: context_sku
          in: query
          deprecated: true
          description: Use `context` instead. Will be removed 2027-01-31.
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/RecommendationList'}

components:
  securitySchemes:
    cookieAuth: {type: apiKey, in: cookie, name: acme_session}
  parameters:
    Locale:
      name: Accept-Language
      in: header
      schema: {type: string, default: en-NL, enum: [en-NL, nl-NL, de-DE, fr-FR, en-GB]}
  responses:
    NotFound:
      description: Not found
    Problem:
      description: RFC 9457 problem details
      content:
        application/problem+json:
          schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Problem'}
  schemas:
    Price:
      type: object
      required: [amount, currency]
      properties:
        amount: {type: integer, description: "Minor units, e.g. 12995 = €129.95"}
        currency: {type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3}$', example: EUR}
        was: {type: [integer, 'null'], description: Strike-through price for the PDP badge}
        promo:
          type:
            - string
            - "null"
    Product:
      type: object
      properties:
        slug: {type: string}
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 120}
        badges:
          type: array
          items: {type: string, enum: [new, eco, bestseller, "last-chance", '-30%']}
        variants:
          type: array
          items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Variant'}
    Variant:
      type: object
      properties:
        sku: {type: string, example: "AUR-2-BLK-42"}
        color: {type: string}
        size: {type: string, description: 'EU size as a string, so "42.5" and "XL" both work'}
        price: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
        stock: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    Cart:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string, format: uuid}
        items: {type: array, items: {type: object}}
        subtotal: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
        free_shipping_remaining: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Price'}
    RecommendationList:
      type: object
      properties:
        slot: {type: string}
        strategy: {type: string, enum: [personalized, bestsellers, similar-items]}
        items: {type: array, items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Product'}}
        model_version: {type: string, example: two_tower_v3@2026-11-01}
    Problem:
      type: object
      properties:
        type: {type: string, format: uri}
        title: {type: string}
        status: {type: integer}
        detail: {type: string}

# Changelog

All notable changes to **@acme/storefront** are documented here.
The format is (loosely 😅) based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) — except for the CSS, which adheres to nothing.

<!-- 
  Marketing folks: please add customer-facing notes under "Highlights". 
  Engineers: keep the PR links, the release bot scrapes them for the #launches post.
-->

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- ✨ Klarna "Pay in 3" badge on the PDP for orders between €35 and €1.500 ([#2291](https://github.com/acme/storefront/pull/2291))
- Mini-cart shows a free-shipping progress bar; the threshold comes from the CMS (`site_settings.free_shipping_threshold`), so marketing can change it without a deploy 
* `useRecommendations()` hook now accepts `{ slot, limit, fallback }`
- - [ ] screenshot of the Klarna badge for the release notes (@marketing)
### Fixed
- 🐛 Category grid showed `NaN` as the price for bundles with 0 components (#2304)
- Fixed CLS on the mobile PDP gallery — LCP went from 3.1s → 2.2s on the throttled Moto G4 profile


## [4.12.0] - 2026-11-03

### Highlights 🎄
> Black Friday prep release. Everything is feature-flagged; marketing can toggle it in the CMS under **Settings → Campaigns**.

* New **countdown banner** for the homepage hero, with a proper `<time>` element and a timezone-aware end date
* "Last chance" badge when stock < 5
    * only for SKUs with `inventory.track = true`
    * colour is `--color-badge-urgent` (#D7263D), approved by design in FIG-812
* Gift cards: €25 / €50 / €100 + custom amount (min €10, max €500)

### Price changes

The pricing team asked us to log these here as well as in the pricing sheet:

SKU | Product | Old price | New price | Change
:-- | --- | --: | --: | :-:
AUR-2-BLK-42 | Aurora Runner 2 (black) | €129,95 | €119,95 | ▼ 7.7%
AUR-2-WHT-43 | Aurora Runner 2 (white) | €129,95 | €119,95 | ▼ 7.7%
TEE-1-WHT-M | Organic tee | €19,95 | €22,95 | ▲ 15%
GFT-CARD-25 | Gift card €25 | €25,00 | €25,00 | —
HOM-MUG-SET4 | Stoneware mug set (4) | €34,99 | €29,99 | ▼ 14.3%

### Changed
- **BREAKING:** `formatPrice(amount, currency)` now expects **minor units** (cents). Migrate like this:

  ```diff
  - formatPrice(129.95, 'EUR')
  + formatPrice(12995, 'EUR')
  ```

- Upgraded Next.js 14.2 → 15.0.3; the `next/image` `domains` option is replaced by `remotePatterns` (see `next.config.mjs`)
-   Recs carousel moved behind `<Suspense>`; the skeleton now matches the card height, so no more layout jump when recommendations load slowly on 3G

### Fixed
1. Coupon field accepted lowercase codes but validation was case-sensitive (`bf26-10` ≠ `BF26-10`)
2. Safari 16 crashed on `structuredClone` in the wishlist — polyfilled
3) Off-by-one in pagination on `/c/[slug]?page=N` when N > 9

## 4.11.2 (2026-10-21)

### Fixed
- hotfix: VAT rounding for NL — prices like €9.995 were rounding *down* (banker's rounding 🙃); now half-up, see `pricing/rounding.md`
- hotfix: `hreflang` tags on marketing landing pages pointed to staging
## [4.11.0] - 2026-10-07
### Added
+ PDP: size guide modal pulls its tables from the CMS (`size_guide` rich-text block). Supports `<table>` HTML from the editor
+ A/B test hooks for recs: `two_tower_v3` vs `control` (50/50), tracked via the `recs_impression` + `recs_click` GA4 events
+ Storybook stories for `<PriceTag>`, `<StockBadge>`, `<CountdownBanner>`
### Deprecated
- `<ProductCard variant="legacy">` — will be removed in 5.0
### Removed
- Dropped the IE11 polyfills (finally 🎉🎉)

<details>
<summary>Dependency bumps (23)</summary>

- next 14.2.13 → 14.2.15
- react-aria-components 1.3.3 → 1.4.0
- @stripe/stripe-js 4.5.0 → 4.8.0
- ...and 20 more by renovate[bot]

</details>

## [4.10.0] - 2026-09-15

### Added
* Headless CMS preview mode: editors can open drafts via `/api/preview?secret=…&slug=…`  
  (the preview cookie lasts 1 hour)
* Promo code field on the cart page
  - stacks with member prices only for codes with the `VIP-` prefix
    - e.g. `VIP-SUMMER15`
      - (yes, this nesting is getting silly)

### Security
- Bumped `sharp` to 0.33.5[^sharp]

<!-- fmt: skip -->
- contributors:   @maya-k   @tbecker   @lena.vos   @renovate[bot]
  (generated by the release bot -- do not reflow)

[^sharp]: Only exploitable via user-uploaded images, which we don't allow on the storefront. CMS uploads *were* affected, so the CMS got patched the same day.

Older entries live in [docs/CHANGELOG-2025.md](docs/CHANGELOG-2025.md).

input.content: --- title: "Contributing" linkTitle: Contributing weight: 90 description: > How to propose changes to the Acme marketing site and the shared CMS content models -- for engineers *and* for the marketing team. aliases: [/docs/contributing/, "/how-to-help"] tags: - process - onboarding --- # Contributing to acme-marketing 👋 Thanks for helping out! This repo powers **www.acme-shop.example** (marketing pages, campaign landing pages, the blog) and holds the content-model definitions for our headless CMS. Engineers, designers, copywriters and the occasional intern all commit here, so the rules below are deliberately boring. {{% pageinfo color="warning" %}} **Code freeze:** no merges to `main` between **Nov 24 and Dec 2** (Black Friday / Cyber Monday) unless it's a P1 fix approved in #web-incidents. {{% /pageinfo %}} ## TL;DR 1. Branch off `main` (`feat/…`, `fix/…`, `copy/…`) 1. `pnpm i && pnpm dev` → http://localhost:4321 1. Open a PR, fill in the template, tag **@acme/web-reviewers** 1. Wait for ✅ checks + 1 approval (2 for anything touching `src/lib/pricing`) ## Local setup You need Node 20 (we use [Volta](https://volta.sh), it picks the right version automatically), pnpm 9, and Docker if you want the CMS running locally. git clone git@github.com:acme/acme-marketing.git cd acme-marketing pnpm install cp .env.example .env.local # ask in #web-platform for the preview token If `pnpm dev` complains about `sharp`, run `pnpm rebuild sharp`. It's always sharp. The `Makefile` wraps the common stuff: ```make dev: ⇥pnpm dev --host seed: ⇥docker compose exec cms npm run seed -- --locale=en,nl,de ``` ## Commits & branches We use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). The release bot reads them, so a typo = a missing changelog entry. | type | when | example | |------|------|---------| | `feat` | new page, component, CMS field | `feat(landing): add BF26 hero variant B` | | `fix` | bug | `fix(pricing): show €0,00 as "Free"` | | `copy` | text-only change by marketing | `copy(home): new USP strip wording` | | `chore` | deps, CI | `chore: bump astro to 4.16` | | `perf` | | `perf(img): serve AVIF for the hero` | ## Writing content (marketing team 💜) Most pages are Markdown with front matter in `src/content/`. Things that bite people: * **Prices** never go into copy as plain text. Use the shortcode so they update when the pricing team changes them: `{{< price sku="AUR-2-BLK-42" >}}` renders "€119,95" (or "~~€129,95~~ €119,95" during a promo). * Emoji are fine in headings and CTAs, max **one** per heading 🙏. No emoji in `` or the meta description -- Google strips some of them and it looks broken in the SERPs. * UTM parameters: lowercase, hyphens, no spaces → `utm_campaign=bf26-early-access`. - Links to products: use the slug, not the full URL (`/p/aurora-runner-2`); the build checks them. - external links get `rel="noopener"` automatically + Images: max 400 KB, WebP or AVIF, and **always** fill in `alt`. Decorative images get `alt=""`. Email templates live in `emails/` and use Liquid. Personalisation tokens like {{ customer.first_name | default: "there" }} and {{ cart.item_count }} are rendered by the ESP, not by us, and so are conditionals such as {% if customer.vip %}early access{% endif %} -- don't wrap them in backticks in the source or they'll end up in the inbox literally. {{< alert title="Heads up" color="info" >}} The CMS **content models** (`cms/models/*.json`) are code. Renaming a field breaks the storefront build until both PRs are merged, so coordinate in #web-platform first. {{< /alert >}} > **Tip:** landing pages can override the nav and the promo banner from front matter: > > ```yaml > title: "Black Friday 2026" > banner: {text: "Up to 40% off 🎉", variant: urgent ,ends_at: 2026-11-28T23:59:00+01:00} > nav: > hide: [ blog, about ] > ``` > > Anything else needs a component change. <p align="center"> <img src="docs/img/content-workflow.png" alt="Diagram: copy is written in Google Docs, pasted into the CMS, checked in preview mode, then published" width="640"> </p> ## Glossary PDP : Product detail page, `/p/{slug}`. PLP : Product listing page -- category grids and search results. SKU : Stock keeping unit. Format `FAM-GEN-COLOR-SIZE`, e.g. `AUR-2-BLK-42`; the size segment can be 1–3 characters. AOV : Average order value. Revenue ÷ orders, **excluding** gift cards and shipping. ## Pull request checklist - [ ] Screenshots (desktop **and** mobile) for visual changes - [ ] Lighthouse ≥ 90 on the changed page (`pnpm lh -- --url=/your-page`) - [x] I read this file - [ ] Copy reviewed by someone in #marketing-copy (legal-ish text: also tag @legal-web) - [ ] No hard-coded prices, SKUs or campaign dates - [ ] if you *really* need a date, put it in `src/data/campaigns.yaml` ## Code of conduct Be kind. We're a small team and everyone is busy in Q4. See [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)[^coc]. [^coc]: Adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 2.1. Report problems to people-team@acme-shop.example, not in Slack.

Acme Storefront 🛍️

The Next.js storefront, headless-CMS integration & recommendation widgets behind acme-shop.example

[![CI](https://github.com/acme/storefront/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/acme/storefront/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/acme/storefront/branch/main/graph/badge.svg?token=AbC123xYz)](https://codecov.io/gh/acme/storefront) [![Lighthouse perf](https://img.shields.io/badge/lighthouse-94-brightgreen?logo=lighthouse)](https://lighthouse.acme-shop.example) ![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D20-339933?logo=node.js&logoColor=white) ![pnpm](https://img.shields.io/badge/pnpm-9-F69220?logo=pnpm&logoColor=white) [![Storybook](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/storybookjs/brand@main/badge/badge-storybook.svg)](https://storybook.acme-shop.example)
> [!IMPORTANT] > **Code freeze:** Nov 24 – Dec 2 (BF/CM). Only P1 fixes, approved in `#web-incidents`. ## Table of contents - [What's in here](#whats-in-here) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Environment](#environment) - [Pricing & SKUs](#pricing--skus) - [Recommendations](#recommendations) - [Deploying](#deploying) - [FAQ](#faq) What's in here -------------- ``` apps/ storefront/ Next.js 15 (app router) -- the shop marketing/ Astro landing pages + blog packages/ ui/ React components + Storybook pricing/ formatPrice, rounding, VAT cms-client/ typed client for the headless CMS services/ recs/ FastAPI recommendation service (python) ``` ## Quick start **Prereqs:** Node ≥ 20, pnpm 9, Docker Desktop (for CMS + Postgres + recs). ```bash pnpm install docker compose up -d cms db redis recs # ~2 min the first time ☕ pnpm --filter @acme/storefront dev ``` Then open . Log in to the CMS at http://localhost:1337/admin with `admin@acme.test` (password is in 1Password → *Web / CMS local*). Press Ctrl + Shift + P → **Toggle price debug overlay** to see which promo rule produced a price. Super handy when marketing asks "why is this €3 cheaper on mobile??" ## Environment | Variable | Required | Default | Description | |:---------|:--------:|---------|-------------| | `NEXT_PUBLIC_CMS_URL` | ✅ | `http://localhost:1337` | Public CMS URL (also used by the image loader) | | `CMS_API_TOKEN` | ✅ | — | Read-only token, get it from 1Password → *Web / CMS* | | `RECS_URL` | | `http://localhost:8081/v1` | Recommendation service | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_CURRENCY` | | `EUR` | One of `EUR`, `GBP`, `SEK` | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD` | | `49.00` | In **major** units here (legacy 🙈) | | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | ✅ prod | | Never commit this. Seriously. | ## Pricing & SKUs Prices are stored in **minor units**. `formatPrice(12995, 'EUR', 'nl-NL')` → `€ 129,95`. Rounding rules per market:
MarketEnds inExample
🇳🇱 NL / 🇩🇪 DE,95€ 119,95
🇬🇧 UK.99£ 99.99
🇸🇪 SEwhole kronor1 299 kr
Sample catalogue used by the seed script & Storybook: | SKU | Product | Price (EUR) | Stock | Badge | |----------------|-----------------------------|------------:|------:|--------------| | AUR-2-BLK-42 | Aurora Runner 2 — black | 119,95 | 14 | `-8%` | | AUR-2-WHT-43 | Aurora Runner 2 — white | 119,95 | 0 | sold out | | TEE-1-WHT-M | Organic tee \| white, M | 22,95 | 230 | 🌱 eco | | HOM-MUG-SET4 | Stoneware mug set (4) | 29,99 | 41 | | | GFT-CARD-50 | Gift card | 50,00 | ∞ | 🎁 | SKU anatomy: `AUR-2-BLK-42` = family `AUR` · generation `2` · colour `BLK` · size `42`. Sizes are *strings* (`42.5`, `XL`, `OS` for one-size), never numbers -- `parseInt("42.5")` already cost us one very confused customer. Promo prices by campaign (from `packages/pricing/fixtures/promos.json`): Campaign | SKU | Regular | Promo | Depth --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: BF26 early access | AUR-2-BLK-42 | €129,95 | €103,95 | 20 % BF26 early access | HOM-MUG-SET4 | €34,99 | €24,49 | 30 % CM26 | TEE-1-WHT-M | €22,95 | €17,95 | 22 % ## Recommendations The carousels (`pdp-similar`, `cart-upsell`, `home-for-you`) call `services/recs` through the BFF. Locally the recs service serves a **fake model** that returns bestsellers, unless you set `RECS_MODEL=two_tower_v3` and have AWS credentials for the model bucket.
How do I debug a weird recommendation? 🤔 1. Add `?recs_debug=1` to any URL — each card gets a tooltip with score + strategy 2. Check the `X-Recs-Model` response header 3. Still weird? Post the URL and a screenshot in `#recs-help`. Include your **segment** (shown in the debug overlay), otherwise we can't reproduce it.
## Deploying * PRs → Vercel preview, the URL is posted by the bot * `main` → staging (automatic) * tag `storefront@x.y.z` → production 🚀 ```bash pnpm changeset version && git push --follow-tags ``` * Hotfix? Branch from the tag, see [docs/hotfix.md](docs/hotfix.md). > [!WARNING] > Don't deploy on Fridays after 15:00 CET unless you're also on call this weekend. :pray: ## FAQ **Why is the price different in Storybook?** Storybook uses the seed catalogue above, not live pricing. :shrug: **Can marketing change banner text without a deploy?** Yes! Banners, USPs and the countdown live in the CMS (*Settings → Campaigns*). Changes go live within 60 s thanks to ISR[^isr]. **Who do I ask about…** + pricing → @acme/pricing + CMS models → @acme/web-platform + recommendations → @acme/recs-squad (Slack: `#recs-help`) [^isr]: Incremental Static Regeneration -- pages revalidate every 60 seconds; product pages also revalidate on demand via a CMS webhook. *** Made with ☕ and too many `console.log`s by the Acme Web team · we're hiring

--- title: "Recs A/B test: `two_tower_v3` vs. control" subtitle: 'PDP "You might also like" carousel · Oct 14 – Nov 10, 2026' author: - name: Lena Vos affiliation: Recs squad - name: "Tom Becker" affiliation: Growth marketing date: 2026-11-14 date-format: "D MMMM YYYY" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 code-fold: true code-summary: "Show the code" theme: [cosmo, assets/acme.scss] embed-resources: true fig-width: 8 fig-height: 4.5 execute: echo: false warning: false jupyter: python3 bibliography: refs.bib editor_options: markdown: wrap: 80 canonical: true --- ::: {.callout-important} ## TL;DR for the Monday marketing sync `two_tower_v3` lifted carousel CTR by **+18.4 %** and carousel add-to-cart by __+9.7 %__, with no measurable change in overall conversion. We recommend rolling it out to 100 % of PDP traffic _before_ Black Friday (Nov 27). 🚀 ::: ## Setup Traffic was split 50/50 by `hash(user_id) % 100` in the BFF; logged-out shoppers were bucketed by the `acme_anon` cookie. We excluded staff accounts, bots (CDN bot score < 30) and the Oct 22 outage window (14:05–15:40 CET). See @sec-caveats for everything else that went sideways. Bootstrap CIs follow @efron1994 [ch. 13], and we used CUPED [@deng2013; @xie2016] with pre-period carousel CTR as the covariate^[Pre-period: Sep 16 – Oct 13. Users without pre-period data got the arm mean, which is a bit lazy.]. ```{python} #| label: setup #| include: false import pandas as pd import numpy as np import plotly.express as px from scipy import stats events = pd.read_parquet("data/recs_ab_events.parquet") orders = pd.read_parquet('data/orders_oct_nov.parquet') ``` ```{python} #| fmt: skip #| label: power #| echo: false # hand-aligned on purpose, these go into the appendix verbatim mde = 0.05 # relative alpha = 0.05 power = 0.80 n_per_arm = 41_250 ``` ## Results ```{python} #| label: tbl-funnel #| tbl-cap: Carousel funnel per arm (unique users, not sessions) #| tbl-colwidths: [30,20,20,30] funnel = (events.groupby(["arm", "event"]).user_id.nunique().unstack() .assign(ctr=lambda d: d.click / d.impression, atc_rate=lambda d: d.add_to_cart / d.click)) funnel.style.format({"ctr": "{:.2%}", "atc_rate": "{:.2%}"}) ``` ```{python} #| label: fig-ctr #| fig-cap: "Daily carousel CTR by arm" #| fig-subcap: ["Desktop","Mobile web"] #| fig-alt: "Two line charts of daily carousel click-through rate per arm, desktop on the left and mobile web on the right; two_tower_v3 is above control on every day except the October 22 outage." #| layout-ncol: 2 #| echo: True daily = events.query("event in ['impression', 'click']").pivot_table(index=["day","arm","device"], columns="event", values="user_id", aggfunc="nunique") for device in ["desktop", "mobile"]: d = daily.xs(device, level="device").assign(ctr=lambda x: x.click / x.impression).reset_index() px.line(d, x="day", y="ctr", color="arm", markers=True, template="simple_white").show() ``` Lift is computed per user and bootstrapped with 10 000 resamples: $$ \text{lift} = \frac{\overline{\text{CTR}}_{\text{treatment}} - \overline{\text{CTR}}_{\text{control}}}{\overline{\text{CTR}}_{\text{control}}} $$ The SKUs the new model pushed hardest, by attributed revenue: | Rank | SKU | Product | Price | Attributed revenue | Δ vs. control | |---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | `AUR-2-BLK-42` | Aurora Runner 2, black | €119.95 | €48,210 | +31 % | | 2 | `HOM-MUG-SET4` | Stoneware mug set (4) | €29.99 | €21,977 | +54 % | | 3 | `TEE-1-WHT-M` | Organic tee, white | €22.95 | €18,402 | +12 % | | 4 | `BAG-3-OLV-OS` | Canvas weekender, olive | €89.00 | €15,130 | −4 % | : Top carousel SKUs, Oct 14 – Nov 10 {#tbl-top-skus} ![Daily carousel CTR for control and two_tower_v3 (static export for the PDF version).](figures/ctr_daily.png){#fig-ctr-static fig-alt="Line chart of daily click-through rate on the PDP carousel from 14 October to 10 November 2026, comparing the control arm with the two_tower_v3 arm; the treatment is higher on 27 of 28 days." width=90%} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### By device Mobile web carries ~68 % of PDP traffic, so most of the absolute gain comes from there, even though the _relative_ lift is larger on desktop (+22.1 % vs. +16.9 %). ### By segment | segment | users | CTR control | CTR v3 | |---|--:|--:|--:| | new | 212,400 | 2.9 % | 3.6 % | | returning | 98,750 | 4.4 % | 5.1 % | | VIP | 6,120 | 6.0% | 6.2% | ::: ```{=html}
CTR +18.4% ATC +9.7% CR ±0.0%
``` ## Caveats {#sec-caveats} ::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"} ## Things that went sideways - Oct 22: the recs service was down for 95 min → both arms fell back to bestsellers. Excluded. - The "Autumn Edit" email (Oct 30) drove 3× normal PDP traffic, mostly to **mugs** ☕, which inflates the HOM-* numbers for both arms. * we did _not_ re-weight for this * (maybe we should? @lena) - Safari ITP drops `acme_anon` after 7 days, so ~6 % of logged-out users may have switched arms. ::: ```{mermaid} flowchart LR PDP[PDP page] --> BFF --> R[recs service] R -->|cache miss| M[(two_tower_v3)] R -->|timeout > 150 ms| B[bestsellers fallback] ``` {{< pagebreak >}} ## Recommendation 1. Roll `two_tower_v3` out to 100 % of PDP traffic on **Nov 18**. 2. Keep `control` warm as a fallback during BF/CM (Nov 27 – Dec 1). 3. Next test: the `cart-upsell` slot, same model, starting Dec 8. {{< video https://videos.acme-shop.example/recs/carousel-v3-demo.mp4 title="Demo: the new carousel on staging" >}} ## References ::: {#refs} :::

--- title: "BF/CM 2025 Retrospective: Email, Paid Social & On-site Promos" subtitle: 'Input for the 2026 campaign plan (v0.3, DRAFT -- please do not forward)' author: - "M. de Groot, Growth Marketing" - "S. Okafor, Web Analytics" date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %b %Y')`" output: html_document: toc: yes toc_float: true number_sections: false df_print: kable code_folding: hide pdf_document: default params: start: 2025-11-21 end: 2025-12-02 currency: "EUR" bibliography: [refs.bib] editor_options: chunk_output_type: console markdown: wrap: sentence --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=FALSE, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, dpi=150} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE) library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(scales) orders <- readr::read_csv("data/orders_bfcm_2025.csv") spend <- readr::read_csv("data/paid_social_spend.csv") eur <- label_dollar(prefix = "€", big.mark = ".", decimal.mark = ",") ``` # 1. Executive summary BF/CM 2025 (Fri. Nov. 28 through Cyber Monday, Dec. 1) generated `r eur(sum(orders$net_revenue))` in net revenue, i.e. approx. 2.3x a normal four-day period and +14.6% vs. BF/CM 2024. Average order value (AOV) rose from €71.40 to €78.95, mostly because the "Bundle & Save" promo (3 items for the price of 2.5, e.g. socks, tees and mugs) pushed the average basket from 2.1 to 2.6 items. Conversion rate was flat at 3.9% on desktop but dropped to 2.2% on mobile web, which we attribute to the checkout outage on Sat. Nov. 29 between 10:12 a.m. and 11:47 a.m. CET (see Sec. 4.2 for the incident write-up by Dr. Patel's team). Paid social ROAS came in at 4.1 vs. a target of 5.0; Meta (Instagram + Facebook) was approx. 1.6 pts below plan, while TikTok over-delivered with a ROAS of 6.3, albeit on a small budget of ca. €18.5k. The U.K. store is excluded from all figures because it ran on the old platform until Jan. 2026. Email remained our strongest channel by far. The "Early Access" send to VIP members on Wed. Nov. 26 (approx. 41,200 recipients) had an open rate of 48.7% and a click rate of 9.2%! The subject-line test ("🔥 Your early access starts now" vs. "Psst... your BF prices are ready") was won by the second variant at p = 0.03, though the effect size was small (+0.8 pp). Was the emoji to blame? Probably not; Litmus showed it rendering as an empty box in Outlook 2016, which accounts for ca. 7% of the VIP list. We also learned that sending at 6:00 a.m. instead of 9:00 a.m. made no real difference (the St. Nicholas promo on Dec. 5–6 showed the same pattern, cf. Fig. 4). ## 1.1 What we'd keep, change and drop - **Keep: Bundle & Save.** It worked. Approx. 31% of orders contained a bundle, and margin per order was only 1.2 pts lower than for full-price orders, mostly due to the mug set (SKU HOM-MUG-SET4, reg. €34.99). - **Change: the free-shipping threshold.** We lowered it from €49 to €35 for the weekend. This cost approx. €22.4k in shipping subsidies vs. an estimated €61k in incremental revenue, i.e. a net positive, but see the caveat in Sec. 5 re. return rates. * **Drop: the sitewide countdown banner.** Ms. Alvarez from Brand asked whether it hurt LCP. It did, by ca. 180 ms on mobile (p75), which is still within budget... but it also pushed the hero CTA below the fold on iPhone SE-sized screens. Not worth it. # 2. On-site promotions The table below lists the top SKUs by net revenue during the promo window (Nov. 21 – Dec. 2). Prices are incl. VAT; "BF price" is the lowest price shown at any point, not the average. Gift cards are listed for completeness only. | SKU | Product | Reg. price | BF price | Units | Net revenue | |---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:| | AUR-2-BLK-42 | Aurora Runner 2, black | €129.95 | €103.95 | 1,284 | €110,310 | | HOM-MUG-SET4 | Stoneware mug set (4) | €34.99 | €24.49 | 3,950 | €79,940 | | TEE-1-WHT-M | Organic tee, white, M | €22.95 | €17.95 | 2,210 | €32,780 | | GFT-CARD-50 | Gift card €50 | €50.00 | €50.00 | 870 | n/a^1^ | ^1^ Gift cards are counted when redeemed, not when sold. ```{r revenue-by-day, fig.cap="Net revenue per day, BF/CM 2025 vs. 2024. Dashed line = 2024.", fig.alt="Line chart of daily net revenue in euros for both years", out.width="100%"} orders |> count(day = as.Date(created_at), year, wt = net_revenue) |> ggplot(aes(day, n, linetype = factor(year))) + geom_line() + scale_y_continuous(labels = eur) ``` Fig. 1 shows the usual shape: a spike on Friday at approx. 9 a.m., a dip on Saturday (the outage), and a long tail on Monday that peaks after 8 p.m. In 2024 the Monday peak was ca. 25% lower. We think the difference is mostly the "Cyber Monday Extra" email at 7:30 p.m., which had the best revenue per send of the whole campaign (€0.41 vs. a campaign avg. of €0.17). The vs. 2024 comparison is not like-for-like, though: in 2024 BF fell on Nov. 29, so the pre-BF "early access" window was one day shorter. > "Don't run another sitewide 30% off. Run fewer, deeper, category-specific deals." -- J. Smith, VP E-commerce, in the Dec. 4 debrief. We agree in principle. However, the data in Fig. 3 suggest that category deals cannibalised full-price sales in adjacent categories by approx. 6–9%, so "fewer, deeper" isn't free either. # 3. Paid social ```{r paid-social-roas, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, cache=TRUE} spend |> group_by(channel) |> summarise(roas = sum(attributed_revenue) / sum(spend)) |> ggplot(aes(reorder(channel, roas), roas)) + geom_col() + coord_flip() ``` Total paid social spend was €212k (Meta €171k, TikTok €18.5k, Pinterest €22.5k), i.e. approx. 9% over the original plan because the Meta budget was raised by 15% on Thu. Nov. 27 at 4 p.m. after a promising first day of early access. In hindsight that was a mistake: CPMs on Meta roughly doubled from Thu. to Fri. (from €6.10 to €12.40), and the extra budget mostly bought expensive impressions for people who'd already been reached 4–5 times. TikTok, on the other hand, was capped at €2k/day and hit the cap every day by noon. Should we have raised the TikTok cap instead? Probably yes, although the attribution window there is 7-day click / 1-day view, vs. Meta's 7-day click only, so the numbers aren't directly comparable (see the appendix of the Q3 report, pp. 12–14). ::: {.alert .alert-warning} **Attribution caveat.** All ROAS figures use platform-reported conversions, de-duplicated against GA4 with a 24 h window. They are almost certainly too optimistic, e.g. Meta claims 1.2M in revenue but GA4 last-click attributes only €640k to Meta. Use them for relative comparisons, not absolutes. ::: # 4. Incidents ## 4.2 Checkout outage, Sat. Nov. 29 The payment provider's 3-D Secure endpoint returned HTTP 502 for approx. 95 min. Checkout fell back to "try again later" instead of offering PayPal or iDEAL, which it should have done per the runbook (No. 7, "PSP degradation"). Estimated lost revenue: €48k–€63k, depending on how many of the 2,140 abandoned checkouts would have converted at the usual 31% rate. The fix (automatic fallback to alternative payment methods) shipped in storefront v4.12.0 on Nov. 3 of this year.\ Dr. Patel's full write-up is in Confluence; the short version is "test the fallback before the peak, not during it". # 5. Recommendations for 2026 1. Start early access on **Mon. Nov. 23** instead of Wed., and send it to the full VIP list (approx. 44k by then) at 7 a.m. CET. Keep the subject line short, emoji optional. 2. Keep Bundle & Save, but cap the mug set at 2 bundles per order. Last year one customer in Utrecht ordered 41 of them, which is, frankly, impressive. 3. Budget paid social by marginal ROAS, not by channel share. Concretely: start TikTok at €4k/day and move budget daily, not weekly. 4. Run a proper free-shipping threshold test (€35 vs. €49) in Oct., not during BF/CM itself, so we can measure the effect on return rates as well[^returns]. 5. Ask the U.S. team (Acme Retail Inc.) how they handled Thanksgiving week; their AOV was up 19.3% with much shallower discounts. [^returns]: Return rates for orders placed during BF/CM were 24.1% vs. 17.8% in a normal week. Orders that only crossed the free-shipping threshold because of a low-value add-on (e.g. a €4.95 pair of socks) were returned far more often. We have not yet checked whether this is causal.
Prepared by Growth Marketing & Web Analytics, Acme Retail B.V. Figures as of Dec. 3, 2025, 11:00 a.m.; preliminary until Finance closes the month.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 # -*- coding: utf-8 -*- # fmt: markdown """ # merch_digest.py Builds the **weekly merchandising digest** for the web, buying and marketing teams: top movers by revenue, the SKUs the recommender is pushing hardest, and a short LLM-written intro for the `#merch-weekly` Slack channel. Run it as a plain script (`python merch_digest.py --week 2026-W46`) or render it with Quarto (`quarto render merch_digest.py`) to get the HTML version with charts. * needs `ACME_WAREHOUSE_DSN`, `LLM_API_KEY` and (for `--post`) `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` * safe to re-run -- it only *reads* from the warehouse * ...and only posts to Slack with `--post` """ # %% #| label: setup #| echo: false #| warning: FALSE #| tags: [ parameters ] from __future__ import annotations import argparse import datetime as dt import json import os from dataclasses import dataclass import pandas as pd WEEK = "2026-W46" # overridden by --week or by Quarto params CURRENCY = "EUR" TOP_N = 15 BANNED_WORDS = ["drop","steal","insane","must-have"] # fmt: skip # fmt: off PRICE_BANDS = { # band min max label "entry": ( 0.00, 24.99, "under €25"), "core": ( 25.00, 79.99, "€25–80"), "premium": ( 80.00, 199.99, "€80–200"), "luxe": ( 200.00, 99999.0, "€200+"), } # fmt: on # fmt: markdown # ### Why the price bands look odd # # Buying wanted "€25–80" instead of "€25–79.99" because it *reads* better in the deck. The bands are inclusive on both ends, so a €79.99 tee is `core` and an €80.00 sneaker is `premium`. # Don't change them without asking @buying-team. @dataclass class Mover: sku: str name: str price: float revenue: float wow: float # week-over-week change, 0.12 == +12 % recs_share: float = 0.0 # share of revenue attributed to recs carousels def as_row(self) -> str: arrow = "▲" if self.wow >= 0 else "▼" return f"| `{self.sku}` | {self.name} | €{self.price:,.2f} | €{self.revenue:,.0f} | {arrow} {abs(self.wow):.0%} | {self.recs_share:.0%} |" # %% [markdown] # fmt: markdown # ## Data # # Revenue comes from `marts.fct_order_lines` (net of returns, **excl. VAT**), recs exposure from `recs.impressions_daily`. Gift cards and shipping lines are excluded because they wreck every chart. # # * Week boundaries are ISO weeks, Monday 00:00 Europe/Amsterdam # * A "mover" is a SKU whose revenue changed by ≥ 25 % week over week **and** that sold ≥ 20 units # - bundles count once per bundle, not per component # # Known issues: # 1. `recs_share` is `NaN` for SKUs launched mid-week; we fill with 0 # 2. bundles (`BND-*`) are listed under their *first* component. Yes, that's wrong. WEB-4411 # %% #| label: load-data #| code-fold: show #| code-summary: "SQL + loader" #| output: false def load_movers(week: str = WEEK, top_n: int = TOP_N) -> list[Mover]: dsn = os.environ["ACME_WAREHOUSE_DSN"] # fmt: skip sql = """ select sku, product_name, avg_price, revenue, wow_change, coalesce(recs_share, 0) from marts.weekly_sku_movers where iso_week = %(week)s and units >= 20 order by abs(wow_change) desc limit %(top_n)s """ df = pd.read_sql(sql, dsn, params={"week": week, "top_n": top_n}) return [Mover(*row) for row in df.itertuples(index=False)] # %% #| label: fig-movers #| fig-cap: "Week-over-week revenue change, top movers" #| fig-alt: >- #| Horizontal bar chart with one bar per SKU, sorted by week-over-week revenue change; #| green bars are increases, red bars are decreases, and the Aurora Runner 2 is the longest green bar. #| fig-width: 7 #| fig-height: 5 #| column: page-right def plot_movers(movers: list[Mover]): import matplotlib.pyplot as plt movers = sorted(movers, key=lambda m: m.wow) fig, ax = plt.subplots() ax.barh([m.sku for m in movers], [m.wow for m in movers], color=["#2e7d32" if m.wow >= 0 else "#c62828" for m in movers]) ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda x, _: f"{x:+.0%}") ax.set_title(f"Top movers {WEEK}") return fig # fmt: markdown wrap=sentence BLURB_PROMPT = """ You are the voice of **Acme Shop**: warm, a little playful, never pushy. Write the intro for this week's internal merch digest. It goes to the web team, the buyers and the marketing team, so it should be useful to all three. ## Rules - Max. 90 words. No hashtags. At most one emoji. - Mention the #1 mover by name and price, e.g. "the Aurora Runner 2 (€119.95)". - Never invent numbers; only use the table below. - If a SKU is out of stock, say so -- don't hype it. - Banned words: {banned} ## Data {table} """ # fmt: markdown SKU_HELP = r""" **SKU format:** `FAM-GEN-COL-SIZE`, validated with `^[A-Z]{3}-\d+-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9A-Z]{1,3}$`. Sizes are *strings* -- `42`, `42.5`, `XL`, `OS` (one size). Literal asterisks in product names (looking at you, \*NEW\* Aurora) must be escaped. """ # fmt: json SLACK_BLOCKS = """ {"blocks":[{"type":"header","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Merch digest"}}, {"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"PLACEHOLDER"}},{"type":"divider"}]} """ # fmt: html EMAIL_FOOTER = """
Acme Retail B.V. · Keizersgracht 1 · Amsterdam
Unsubscribe
""" def render_digest(movers: list[Mover], blurb: str, week: str = WEEK) -> str: rows = "\n".join(m.as_row() for m in movers) # fmt: markdown return f""" # 🛒 Merch digest -- {week} {blurb} ## Top movers | SKU | Product | Price | Revenue | WoW | via recs | |---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:| {rows} Generated {dt.datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} by `merch_digest.py`. Numbers are net of returns and **exclude VAT**. """ def llm_complete(prompt: str) -> str: # thin wrapper, see acme_ml.llm from acme_ml.llm import complete return complete(prompt, max_tokens=300, temperature=0.4) def post_to_slack(payload: dict) -> None: import urllib.request req = urllib.request.Request(os.environ["SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"], data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) # %% #| label: run #| echo: false #| output: asis def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Weekly merch digest") ap.add_argument("--week", default=WEEK) ap.add_argument("--top-n", type=int, default=TOP_N) ap.add_argument("--post", action="store_true", help="post to #merch-weekly") args = ap.parse_args(argv) movers = load_movers(args.week, args.top_n) table = "\n".join(m.as_row() for m in movers) blurb = llm_complete(BLURB_PROMPT.format(table=table, banned=", ".join(BANNED_WORDS))) digest = render_digest(movers, blurb, args.week) print(digest) if args.post: payload = json.loads(SLACK_BLOCKS) payload["blocks"][1]["text"]["text"] = digest[:2900] post_to_slack(payload) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

#' ---
#' title: "Promo price QA -- BF/CM 2026"
#' author: "Web Analytics (S. Okafor)"
#' date: "2026-11-17"
#' output: html_document
#' ---
#'
#' Checks every promo price exported from the CMS against the pricing rules before a campaign goes live.
#' Run with `Rscript promo_price_check.R bf26-early-access` or render it with `quarto render promo_price_check.R`.

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning:   FALSE
#| include: !expr interactive()
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(stringr)
  library(glue)
})

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE, scipen = 999)
args     <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
campaign <- if (length(args) && !startsWith(args[[1]], "--")) args[[1]] else "bf26-early-access"
strict   <- "--strict" %in% args

# fmt: markdown
# ## Pricing rules (summary)
#
# | market | ends in | max depth |
# |---|---|---|
# | NL, DE, BE | ,95 | 40 % |
# | UK | .99 | 40 % |
# | SE | whole kronor | 30 % |
#
# Source of truth is the **pricing sheet**, not this comment. If they disagree, the sheet wins and somebody should fix this comment.

rules <- tibble::tribble(
  ~market, ~ending, ~max_depth,
  "NL",    0.95,    0.40,
  "DE",    0.95,    0.40,
  "BE",    0.95,    0.40,
  "UK",    0.99,    0.40,
  "SE",    0.00,    0.30
)

# fmt: skip
usage <- r"---(
Usage: Rscript promo_price_check.R <campaign> [--strict]

  campaign   CMS campaign slug, e.g. bf26-early-access
  --strict   exit with status 1 on *any* rule violation      (default: only on errors)
)---"

#| label: load
#| cache: TRUE
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime("data/promo_export.csv")
#| dependson: [ "setup" ]
promos <- read_csv(glue("data/{campaign}/promo_export.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    sku         = str_trim(sku),
    reg_price   = as.numeric(reg_price),
    promo_price = as.numeric(promo_price),
    depth       = round(1 - promo_price / reg_price, 3)
  ) |>
  left_join(rules, by = "market")

check_price_ending <- function(price, ending) {
    cents <- round(price %% 1, 2)
    ifelse(ending == 0, cents == 0, abs(cents - ending) < 1e-9)
}

#| label: checks
#| echo: true
#| results:   'asis'
qa <- promos |>
  mutate(
    bad_ending  = !check_price_ending(promo_price, ending),
    too_deep    = depth > max_depth,
    not_cheaper = promo_price >= reg_price,
    ok = !(bad_ending | too_deep | not_cheaper)
  )

n_bad   <- sum(!qa$ok)
n_total <- nrow(qa)
offenders <- qa |>
  filter(!ok) |>
  arrange(desc(depth)) |>
  head(10) |>
  glue_data("- `{sku}` ({market}): €{format(promo_price, nsmall = 2)} vs. reg. €{format(reg_price, nsmall = 2)}, depth {scales::percent(depth, accuracy = 0.1)}") |>
  paste(collapse = "\n")

# fmt: markdown
alert_body <- "
**Promo QA failed** for campaign `{campaign}` ⚠️

{n_bad} of {n_total} prices break the rules. Worst offenders:

{offenders}

Fix them in the CMS (*Pricing → Promotions*) and re-run the check. Ping #pricing-help if a rule looks wrong -- don't just override it.
"

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
promo_help_md <- r"(
## How to read this table
Each row is one **promo price** from the CMS export. A row turns red when the price breaks a rule: e.g. it doesn't end in `,95`/`.99`, it's *higher* than the regular price, or the discount is deeper than the cap Finance signed off on (40 % for most markets, 30 % for SE).

-   `reg_price` = regular price incl. VAT
-   `promo_price` = what the shopper pays
    - for bundles this is the bundle price, not per item
-   `depth` = 1 - promo/reg, rounded to 3 decimals

Questions → #pricing-help 💬
)"

# fmt: markdown
rules_changelog_md <- R"[
### Rules changelog
* 2026-11-02 -- cap raised from 35 % to 40 % for `HOM-*` (mugs, candles) after the Q3 overstock, see [the decision doc](https://docs.acme-shop.example/pricing/q3-overstock)
* 2026-09-15 -- UK prices must end in `.99`, NL/DE/BE in `,95`
+ 2026-06-01 -- SE switched to whole kronor
]"

# fmt: css
qa_css <- "
.qa-bad{background:#fde8e8;color:#9b1c1c}
.qa-ok {background:#e7f6ec}
table.qa td.num{text-align:right;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
"

#' ## Results
#'
#' `r n_bad` of `r n_total` promo prices break at least one rule.

#| label: tbl-qa
#| tbl-cap: "Promo prices that break a rule"
#| layout: [[1], [1,1]]
qa |>
  filter(!ok) |>
  select(sku, market, reg_price, promo_price, depth, bad_ending, too_deep, not_cheaper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 3, 0, 0, 0))

#| label: gadget
#| eval: false
run_qa_gadget <- function() {
  shiny::shinyApp(
    ui = bslib::page_fluid(
      shiny::tags$style(qa_css),
      shiny::markdown(promo_help_md),
      shiny::markdown(rules_changelog_md),
      DT::DTOutput("qa")
    ),
    server = function(input, output, session) {
      output$qa <- DT::renderDT(DT::datatable(qa, class = "qa") |> DT::formatStyle("ok", target = "row", backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual(c(FALSE, TRUE), c("#fde8e8", "#e7f6ec"))))
    }
  )
}

if (n_bad > 0) {
  message(glue(alert_body))
  if (strict) quit(status = 1)
} else {
  message(glue("✅ {n_total} promo prices for {campaign} look fine. Ship it!"))
}
